problems.title: Polynomial comparison violates zero-outer-trace affine constraint

source_claim.kind: statement, definition application or proof step
source_claim.location: Section7 setup and(7.1) pp34-35; Propositions7.2,7.5,7.6 pp35-40
source_claim.claim: The previously defined minimizer with h inH01 can be used with uncut nonzero Pm or Tm.

problems.assumptions: Pm=x1,m=1,L>R on ellipse E_epsilon(L), or disk. This meets later polynomial and domain hypotheses; comparison with earlier definition is the problem.
problems.counterexample: If V andV-Pm both belong zero-outer-trace H_epsilon,Lambda, Pm has zero trace; x1 does not. Literal admissible class empty. Arbitrary L>0 ellipse also neednot contain fixedDR.
problems.counterevidence: Differential problem(7.2) imposes h only on crack and is wellposed; independently solved Fourier problem uses that consistent formulation.
problems.impact: The zero-outer-trace affine class defined in (7.1) is empty for nonzero unmodified homogeneous P_m or T_m. Propositions 7.2/7.5/7.6 use this undefined minimum in the explicit two-pole asymptotic derivation. The local BVP (7.11) and its correct Fourier solution are counterevidence to a numerical-coefficient error, but do not redefine the written variational object. A cutoff is a required new repair. Major proof-chain defect; no false final coefficient or eigenvalue theorem is claimed.

A cutoff equal1 near the crack preserves local data and domain sandwich and can recover the constants. Severity attaches to the missing substantive variational link, not to a counterexample to the final coefficients.
